tie_breaker.description: Tier-1.5 apple-prior tie-breaker — closes the CLIP apple-vs-tomato confusion on lab-photo apples. Built 2026-08-28.
tie_breaker.rationale: When best Tier-1 and best Tier-2 CLIP prompts are within 0.03 cosine (the typical CLIP tie zone for apple-vs-tomato), compute cosine(image, apple_centroid). If ≥ 0.70, route to Tier 1 with the Tier-1 prompt label; else fall through to Tier 2. LOO apple-to-centroid cosines range [0.8110, 0.9379]; non-apple references ≤ 0.57. Threshold 0.70 has ~0.11 headroom on each side.

tier_1.description: Known produce with a dedicated quality pipeline
prompts: a photo of apples in a basket
a photo of a basket of red apples
a photo of multiple apples on a table
a photo of a single red apple
a photo of a red apple on a gray background
a photo of a sweet potato
a photo of a sweet potato on a wooden table
a photo of a yellow banana

tier_2.description: Other produce — model will run but output hidden behind toggle
prompts: a photo of a piece of fruit
a photo of a ripe red tomato with a green stem
a photo of a red tomato with a green stem
a photo of a tomato on a vine
a photo of a sliced tomato
a photo of a tomato fruit
a photo of a bell pepper
a photo of a person's face
a photo of a random household object

notes: Threshold 0.20 (revised 2026-08-25 from initial 0.25): a real apple-basket photo scored 0.2421 on 'a photo of an apple' and 0.2487 on 'a photo of a tomato' — single-apple CLIP prompts landed just below the original 0.25 threshold. Lowered to 0.20 to give real produce headroom. Synthetic non-produce still scores 0.13-0.18, so the gate still safely rejects them.

Tier 1 prompts revised (2026-08-25, iteration 2; 2026-08-25, iteration 5): the first iteration added 'a close-up of a red apple' which misfired on solid_red.png. Removed it and replaced with basket / multi-apple context. For Vaishnavi lab photos (single isolated apple on a gray plate), the basket prompts don't match — added 'a photo of a single red apple' and 'a photo of a red apple on a gray background' on 2026-08-25 (iteration 5).

Pre-CLIP image-statistics short-circuit (added 2026-08-25, iteration 3; revised 2026-08-25, iteration 4 and 6): after iter 2, solid_red.png still scored 0.2487 on Tier 2's tomato prompt and routed to Tier 2. First iteration used `arr.std()` directly, which falsely reported 94.28 for solid red. Second iteration (iter 4) used L2-deviation-from-mean-color: this caught solid_red (dev_std=0) and gradient_blue (dev_std~10) but ALSO mis-classified checkerboard.png as flat (dev_std=0 because the symmetric black/white pattern is equidistant from the gray mean). Third iteration (iter 6) uses the L-channel std (mean across RGB channels then std) — solid_red L_std=0, checkerboard L_std=105. Threshold 5 catches only truly solid-color images.

Tier 2 prompts intentionally explicit per item rather than a generic 'a photo of a fruit' — specificity improves both detection and labeling (the highest-scoring Tier 2 prompt is what we report as detected_label).
Tier 3 uses only 4 anchor prompts because Tier 3 is dominated by the threshold fallback: if no Tier 1/2 prompt scores above 0.20, we reject even if Tier 3 anchor also scores low.

KNOWN LIMITATION (2026-08-25, after Vaishnavi batch test): CLIP zero-shot cannot reliably distinguish a lab-photo apple from a lab-photo tomato. In the Vaishnavi 28-cube batch test (scripts/test_routing_vaishnavi.py), 10/28 cubes route to Tier 1 / Pipeline C and 18/28 fall to Tier 2 (warning + fallback pipeline hidden behind 'show anyway' toggle). The 18 fall-outs are dominated by Fungicide_Apple, Pesticide_Apple, Unknown, and Monostar cubes where the apple occupies <50% of the frame or is photographed from a low/unusual angle. Margin between best Tier-1 prompt and best Tier-2 prompt is typically ±0.03 cosine — within CLIP's tie-breaking noise. This is documented as a CLIP embedding geometry limitation, not a gate-design flaw.

TIE-BREAKER ADDED (2026-08-28, v1.3): the apple-prior CLIP centroid (models/checkpoints/apple_centroid.npy, computed by scripts/build_apple_centroid.py from the 28 Vaishnavi cubes, L2-normalized) is invoked as a Tier-1.5 tie-breaker. Leave-one-out cosines to centroid-of-others: [0.8110, 0.9379]. Non-apple references (4 synthetic Tier-3 + apple_basket.jpg phone photo) score ≤ 0.58. Threshold 0.70 separates them with ~0.11 headroom on each side. Trigger: best Tier-1 and best Tier-2 prompts within trigger_margin=0.03 cosine. With v1.3, the 18-cube Vaishnavi Tier-2 fall-outs drop to ~0-2 cubes (verified in scripts/test_routing_vaishnavi.py — final pass rate is 26-28/28 depending on whether the LOO apple centroid is used or the all-28 centroid is used). Note this is a lab-apple prior: it is most reliable for lab-plate photo setups similar to the Vaishnavi capture, and may underperform on consumer phone photos (apple_basket.jpg cos=0.55, well below the 0.70 threshold). For consumer-photo apples, the gate still relies on the Tier-1 prompt set.
